description: Represents a business rule that guides AI behavior for a specific business. Each rule has a category code from the catalog (`GET /v3/ai/business_rule_categories`) and, once placed, a topic. Rules can be AI-generated (system) or user-created. For FAQ category rules, the metadata contains structured question and answer fields extracted from the content. Rules can be activated, deactivated, or held in a pending approval state.

uid.description: The unique identifier (UID) of the business rule (e.g., "br-a1b2c3d4-5678-90ef-ghij-klmnopqrstuv"). Assigned automatically by the system upon creation.

business_uid.description: The unique identifier (UID) of the business that owns this rule (e.g., "biz-1234abcd-5678-90ef-ghij-klmnopqrstuv"). Automatically set based on the authenticated token.

content.description: The content or text of the business rule (e.g., "Always use a friendly and professional tone when communicating with clients"). For FAQ rules, this typically contains both the question and answer in a combined format. At most 20,000 characters.

status.description:
The current status of the business rule, controlling whether the AI agent actively uses it.

* `active` - The rule is currently in effect and will be used by the AI agent.
* `pending_approval` - The rule has been suggested (typically by the system) and is awaiting staff review before becoming active.
* `inactive` - The rule has been deactivated and will not be used by the AI agent.

source.description:
Indicates whether the rule was created by the AI system or by a user (staff member). Only an app token that acts for a staff member can set it on create; a staff token always gets `user`.

* `system` - The rule was generated automatically by the AI based on analysis of business conversations.
* `user` - The rule was manually created or edited by a staff member.

created_by_staff_uid.description: The UID of the staff member who created the rule (e.g., "stf-9876wxyz-5432-10ab-cdef-ghijklmnopqr"). Will be null for system-generated rules that have not been manually edited.

updated_by_staff_uid.description: The UID of the staff member who last updated the rule (e.g., "stf-9876wxyz-5432-10ab-cdef-ghijklmnopqr"). Will be null if the rule has never been updated by a staff member.

sort_order.description: Sort order for displaying rules within a category (e.g., 0). Lower values appear first. Rules within the same category are ordered by this field in ascending order.

metadata.description: Additional metadata associated with the rule, at most 4,096 characters when serialized. Only an app token that acts for a staff member can set it; a staff token gets `null`. For FAQ rules, includes structured `question` and `answer` fields. For system-generated rules, may include `confidence`, `reasoning`, and `evidence` from the AI analysis.

question.description: The question part of an FAQ rule (e.g., "What are your business hours?"). Only present for rules with category `faq`.

answer.description: The answer part of an FAQ rule (e.g., "We are open Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM."). Only present for rules with category `faq`.

confidence.description: AI confidence score ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 indicating how confident the system is about this rule (e.g., 0.92). Only present for system-generated rules.

reasoning.description: AI-generated reasoning explaining why this rule was created or suggested (e.g., "Consistent friendly tone observed across 15 client conversations"). Only present for system-generated rules.

evidence.description: Evidence from conversations that supports this rule. Contains quotes and references from actual client-staff interactions.

client_uid.description: The UID of the client involved in the conversation.

message_uid.description: The UID of the specific message used as evidence.

quote.description: A direct quote from the conversation used as evidence.

speaker.description:
Identifies whether the quote is from a staff member or a client.

* `staff` - The quote is from a staff member.
* `client` - The quote is from a client.

created_at.description: The date and time when the business rule was created, in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2024-12-15T10:30:00.000Z").

updated_at.description: The date and time when the business rule was last updated, in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2024-12-16T14:00:00.000Z").

category_code.description: The catalog category code of the rule (e.g., "tone_of_voice", "faq"). The code belongs to a category of the catalog, see `GET /v3/ai/business_rule_categories`. The same code can exist in more than one topic, for example `tone_of_voice` under `reply_to_clients` and under `ai_receptionist`.

topic.description:
The topic of the rule, one of the catalog topics (e.g., "reply_to_clients", "knowledge_and_files" or null). Null until the rule is placed in a topic.

* `reply_to_clients` - Rules for replies to clients.
* `ai_receptionist` - Rules for the AI Receptionist.
* `bizai_chat` - Rules for BizAI Chat.
* `notes` - Rules for note summaries and call transcripts.
* `preferences` - Preferences and priorities that every agent reads.
* `knowledge_and_files` - Knowledge items, FAQ and documents.

title.description: A short title of the rule (e.g., "No price quotes to leads" or null).

description.description: A description of the rule (e.g., "How we answer price questions" or null).

load_mode.description:
The own load mode of the rule (e.g., "always", "search" or null). Null means the default load mode of the catalog category.

* `always` - Agents load the rule with the list.
* `search` - Agents find the rule through search only.

effective_load_mode.description: The own load mode of the rule, or the default load mode of its catalog category when the rule has none (e.g., "always", "search"). A rule without a topic is `always`.

author_type.description:
Who wrote the rule (e.g., "owner", "platform").

* `platform` - The platform generated the rule.
* `partner` - A partner app wrote the rule.
* `owner` - A staff member of the business wrote the rule.
* `owner_via_ai` - A staff member wrote the rule through an AI assistant.

entry_point.description: The entry point that wrote the rule. A client can send it on create and update; `migration` is set only by the migration (e.g., "rules_page", "bizai_chat" or null).

placed_by.description: What chose the topic of the rule: `writer` (the body had `topic`), `entry_point`, `default` (the default topic of the category), `gate` or `migration` (e.g., "default" or null).

confirmed_at.description: When a staff member confirmed the rule, in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-11-09T10:30:00.000Z" or null).

tier.description:
The precedence tier of the rule (e.g., "owner", "inferred").

* `owner` - The author type is `owner`, or `owner_via_ai` with `confirmed_at` set.
* `inferred` - Every other rule.

evidence.description: Where the rule came from. Only an app that acts for a staff member can set it; `copied_from` is set only by the migration and an update keeps it (e.g., {"type": "conversation", "uid": "conv-123"} or null).

conflict_flags.description: The latest verdict of the write gate on the rule (e.g., {"gate_mode": "warn", "gate_status": "passed", "findings": []} or null).

search_aliases.description: Customer phrasings of the rule, used by search (e.g., ["where do I park"] or null).

deleted_at.description: When the rule was deleted. Only the webhook `business_rule/deleted` and the data feed carry it; API reads do not return deleted rules (e.g., "2026-11-09T10:00:00.000Z" or null).

example.content: Always use a friendly and professional tone when communicating with clients

metadata.reasoning: Consistent friendly tone observed across 15 client conversations
